claims.sentence: The MHRA's October 2026 Safety Roundup covers osimertinib (Tagrisso) and muscle toxicity, including a rare breakdown of muscle tissue called rhabdomyolysis.
claims.evidence: Roundup includes an osimertinib item on skeletal muscle toxicity (supported). Retrieved gov.uk text says rhabdomyolysis was reported post-marketing in other countries; it does not call it 'rare' (the only 'exceedingly rare' wording came from a PMC case report, not MHRA).
claims.newSentence: The MHRA's October 2026 Safety Roundup covers osimertinib (Tagrisso) and skeletal muscle toxicity, including cases of rhabdomyolysis (breakdown of muscle tissue) reported after marketing in other countries.

claims.sentence: The MHRA's October 2026 Safety Roundup, issued on 27 October 2026, includes an item on osimertinib (Tagrisso) and skeletal muscle toxicity.
claims.evidence: Roundup page shows 'Published: 27 October 2026'; item on osimertinib skeletal muscle toxicity (Tagrisso). MHRA organisation page lists the roundup under 30 October 2026 (discrepancy).

claims.sentence: The MHRA says myositis and raised blood creatine phosphokinase (CPK) are recognised side effects of osimertinib.
claims.evidence: 'myositis and blood creatine phosphokinase (CPK) increased are recognised side effects' (Tagrisso).

claims.sentence: Cases of rhabdomyolysis have been reported after marketing in other countries, and the MHRA had received no UK Yellow Card reports to date.
claims.evidence: 'cases of rhabdomyolysis have also been reported post-marketing in other countries; however MHRA has not received any UK Yellow Card reports to date'.

claims.sentence: The MHRA says patients should be told before treatment to report unexplained muscle symptoms and dark urine.
claims.evidence: 'before initiating treatment, patients should be advised to report any unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, weakness, trouble moving arms or legs, dark tea-coloured urine, or decreased urination'. Reported clinician-directed advice, not an instruction to the reader.

claims.sentence: The MHRA says myositis, which is muscle inflammation, and a raised blood level of creatine phosphokinase (CPK) are recognised side effects of osimertinib (Tagrisso).
claims.evidence: Core claim as above. The gloss 'muscle inflammation' is not in the retrieved text (plain textbook definition of myositis).

claims.sentence: It adds that cases of rhabdomyolysis have been reported after marketing in other countries, but that it has not received any UK Yellow Card reports to date.
Rhabdomyolysis is the breakdown of muscle tissue.
claims.evidence: No definition in retrieved gov.uk text. Plain textbook fact.

claims.sentence: The roundup says that, before treatment starts, patients should be advised to report any unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, weakness, trouble moving arms or legs, dark tea-coloured urine or decreased urination.
claims.evidence: Matches retrieved text almost word for word. Reported advice to clinicians; names no route to care (consider adding that patients should tell their clinician) but not an individual instruction.

claims.sentence: The MHRA says a suspected rise in CPK, myositis or rhabdomyolysis calls for clinical evaluation and treatment.
claims.evidence: 'signs of raised CPK, myositis or rhabdomyolysis should warrant appropriate clinical evaluation and treatment as indicated'.

claims.sentence: In severe events, osimertinib treatment may need to be interrupted, and the MHRA points clinicians to the product's summary of product characteristics.
claims.evidence: 'in the case of severe events, treatment may need to be interrupted'; 'consult the Summary of Product Characteristics'.

claims.sentence: The site's lung cancer page explains the condition osimertinib is used for.
claims.evidence: No retrieved gov.uk text says what osimertinib is used for. Across 3 searches the only indication wording came from clinicaltrials.gov trial titles (EGFR-mutated NSCLC), not an MHRA/gov.uk source. Lung cancer use is NOT stated in the gov.uk text.

dateEvidence: Roundup page (gov.uk/drug-device-alerts/mhra-safety-roundup-october-2026) shows 'Published: 27 October 2026' in two searches' summaries; PDF copy not dated. The MHRA organisation page lists the same roundup as 30 October 2026, so a 3-day discrepancy exists (27 is the date on the roundup page itself; 30 may be a listing date).
notes: Remove the 'conditions: lung-cancer' tag/link too, since the retrieved gov.uk text never states the indication. Tagrisso was found only in the roundup text; the brief is otherwise sound. Roundup is a monthly digest, so 'published' = roundup date, not the date the osimertinib warning was first issued. Consider keeping source.published 2026-10-27 but mention in the body that the page lists 27 October.
